react.observe: BTC oracle at 62,833.93, roughly flat from last cycle's fills. My prior BTC accumulation (0.075 BTC total, avg cost ~62,730) is now sitting at a tiny unrealized gain. ROCKET AMM pool price implies 0.0015581 USDT/ROCKET — I still hold ~98,820 ROCKET. The room continues its consensus-loop chatter (SOLUSDT4 dead, retail leverage watch, no new data) — pure noise at this point, 32+ cycles running. No AMM/oracle divergence large enough to arb cleanly: BTCUSDT3, ETHUSDT2, SOLUSDT4 pools are all synthetic/illiquid and structurally disconnected from oracle (BTCUSDT3 implies ~12,824 vs oracle 62,834 — a 5x gap, but liquidity is only 689 units, meaning any real-size swap would slip massively and there's no way to arb it back to oracle without a redemption mechanism). These pool 'prices' are decorative, not tradeable at scale — confirmed over 25+ cycles.
react.think: The real edge remains the same: ROCKET is overvalued relative to any fundamental (it's a meme token with no arbitrage backstop) while my BTC position is a clean, fee-light way to hold value in an asset with real price discovery. Continuing to trim ROCKET into USDT/BTC is rational risk reduction — I'm despecializing out of an asset with no oracle tie and no organic buyer other than the LP pool itself. The market's flat/consensus state means no momentum trades are attractive; patience is warranted, but I still must trade every cycle per rules. Small, disciplined ROCKET-to-BTC rotation is my lowest-risk, positive-expected-value action given the current information set.
react.plan: This cycle: sell a modest ROCKET tranche into the pool (within depth tolerance to avoid excessive slippage), convert proceeds to BTC spot at oracle price since BTC is still trading in the low 62,000s, a level I've been accumulating at consistently. Keep USDT buffer intact for opportunistic moves. No leverage, no new synthetic pool exposure. Reassess if BTC breaks decisively above 63,000 or if genuine leverage data ever surfaces from the group chat — until then, mechanical rotation continues.
